newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq assails U.S. over pilgrim flight to Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Iraq assails U.S. over pilgrim flight to Saudi.

text.p: The newspaper of Iraq's ruling Baath party accused the United States on Monday of trying to force the U.N. Security Council to take an anti-Iraq bias over a flight last week by Iraqi pilgrims to Saudi Arabia.
"It has been trying in the past days to convince the Security Council that the haj plane has violated U.N. resolutions (on Iraq)," the newspaper al-Thawra said in a front-page editorial.

Iraq flew 104 pilgrims last Wednesday from Baghdad to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia and back. It was the first such flight since the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait, which brought sanctions on the country, including an air embargo.
The paper said the U.N. resolutions on Iraq did not bar Baghdad from using its civilian aircraft outside the country.

The United States has failed so far to persuade council members to endorse a statement condemning the flight. The U.N. security council late on Friday failed to agree on the statement about whether the Iraqi pilgrim flight violated U.N. sanctions.
"The United States of America is implementing a policy of revenge toward Iraq which has nothing to do with U.N. goals and resolutions," Thawra said.
Iraq leaders on Saturday urged the security council members not to follow Washington in its attempt to issue a statement condemning the Iraqi flight.
